title: Survey for badminton club organisers
opening: I'm Mike Stoker, a badminton player in Milton Keynes and the developer of ePegboard. I'm asking organisers how they run their club sessions and what takes the most effort. Your answers will help me decide what to build and test. It takes about 8 minutes. Giving your club name is optional.
afterSubmission: Thanks for taking part. If you'd like to try ePegboard features in development and give feedback, you can volunteer below. I'll use your email to invite you to testing and follow up on your feedback. You can leave the tester list at any time.

questions.text: Which country is the club in?
Which best describes the club?
options: Session run by a leisure centre or venue

questions.text: Roughly how many players come on a typical night?
How many courts do you usually have?

sections.title: Running the night
sections.header: Thinking about your main regular session over the past four weeks.

questions.text: How are games mostly decided on a club night?
options: The organiser or session runner picks

questions.text: Which formats do you use?
options: Up-and-down courts (winners move up, losers move down)
King or queen of the court

questions.text: How do you use them?
options: We change format during the night
We change format from week to week

questions.text: Would you like to run a wider range of formats than you do now?
options: No, we're happy as we are

questions.text: What stops you?
options: It takes too long to set up on the night
It's hard to keep track of who's playing whom
Players prefer what we do now
Not sure which formats would work

questions.text: How do games usually end?
options: Played to a full score (for example 21)
Played to a shorter score (for example 11 or 15)
Timed rounds of 10 minutes or more

questions.text: How wide is the range of standards on a typical night?
options: Very mixed, from beginners to league players

questions.text: Do you separate players by playing level?
options: Players sort themselves out by level

questions.text: Why do you separate players by level?
How fair is the way games are picked, for the players?

sections.title: Booking and attendance
sections.header: Thinking about your main regular session over the past four weeks.

questions.text: Do players tell you in advance that they're coming?
When do players pay?
What happens if someone turns up without booking?
Of your last four sessions, how many had someone book and then not turn up?

sections.title: Filling sessions
sections.header: Thinking about your main regular session over the past four weeks.

questions.text: Of your last four sessions, how many were so busy that players waited too long between games?
Of your last four sessions, how many had to turn players away because they were full?
Of your last four sessions, how many had a booked court standing empty because too few players came?
Where do most new players hear about you?
options: Badminton England or a national listing

questions.text: Can people come as a guest or drop in?
options: Yes, a few times before they need to join

questions.text: Do new players get a free or cheaper first session?
Is there a standard players need to be to come?
options: A maximum (for example, a beginners' session)

questions.text: When a regular stops coming, what usually happens?
options: We track attendance and get in touch
We notice and get in touch
We notice but don't usually follow up

questions.text: How do players pay?
options: Through an app or booking system

questions.text: Roughly what does a player pay per session?
questions.hint: In your local currency. Leave it blank if membership covers it.

questions.text: Which shuttles do you mainly use?
Does the club take part in competitions?
options: We host external competitions or matches

questions.text: How are league teams picked?
Does the club ever run coaching?
options: Yes, now and then (a few times a year or less)

questions.text: Who delivers it?
